text:
Jen Park: heads up — we just got an ops alert: p95 tail jumped ~300ms around 03:12-03:22 UTC after last rollout. dashboard: /d/infra/latency-microbatch :warning:
Mike Chen: which rollout did we push? admission-tuner v2 or kernel-selector tweak? :thinking_face:
Jen Park: both. admission-tuner v2 (aggressive downscaling) + kernel-selector change that prefers fused kernels for batch_size >= 4. deploys started ~03:00 UTC.
Rahul Singh: sharing profiler snapshot from 03:15 — lots of time in fallback_kernel::dispatch instead of fused_kernel::exec. flamegraph attached.
Jen Park: log excerpt at ~03:14 (truncated):
```
[03:14:05] admission: accepted microbatch size=1 -> dispatch to fallback_kernel
[03:14:05] kvcache: eviction triggered shard=12 used=92% -> miss-rate spike
[03:14:05] kernel-selector: chose fallback_kernel (heuristic mismatch)
[03:14:05] req 0x7f9a: latency 312ms
```
Sam Ortiz: so admission is producing size=1 under normal load? that will force fallback when fused expects >=4.
Mike Chen: admission autotuner saw higher latencies and shrank batch targets to reduce p50, but combined w/ kv evictions we get dithering.
Rahul Singh: pprof of kvcache shows heavy eviction loops + shard lock contention on writes. looks like a noisy-packing tenant caused sequences to blow past expected cache working set.
Jen Park: proposed causal chain: increased eviction -> cache misses -> more fallback_kernel usage -> higher latency -> admission interprets as signal to shrink batches -> smaller microbatches -> more fallback -> feedback loop.
ops-bot: incident INC-20647 created: "microbatch dithering causing tail latency". pager notified.
Mike Chen: immediate mitigations: 1) roll back kernel-selector fused-threshold tweak 2) pin admission-tuner to previous stable thresholds 3) relax kvcache eviction aggressiveness. can we do a canary rollback?
Jen Park: I'll kick off a canary rollback now. deploy-bot: started deploy canary for rollback/INC-20647 at 03:45 UTC :rocket:
Rahul Singh: also recommend increasing kvcache soft limit per-shard from 1GB -> 1.5GB and reduce eviction pressure for 30m while we observe. That should lower miss spikes.
Sam Ortiz: agree. also add simple smoothing to admission controller: only change batch size by at most 1 unit per 30s and require 3 consecutive windows before acting.
Mike Chen: plan: canary rollback monitor 10m. if p95 returns to baseline -> rollout rollback to prod and apply kvcache config change (config-only rollout).
Jen Park: monitoring: adding temporary alert p95 > 200ms for 5m. watching /d/infra/kvcache-miss as well.
Rahul Singh: attaching profiling gist: https://internal/gists/fg-20647 showing fallback spikes and blocked threads.
Jen Park: canary results at 03:55 — p95 on canary dropped from ~410ms to ~120ms, kvcache miss-rate stabilized. proceeding with full rollback.
Mike Chen: good. follow-ups: (A) revert fused-threshold change permanently unless validated with heavy kvcache stress (B) implement admission smoothing & hysteresis (C) add a runbook entry for microbatch oscillations.
Sam Ortiz: I'll open PR for admission smoothing today and add unit + integration tests to simulate kvcache miss bursts.
Rahul Singh: I'll run a synthetic noisy-packing stress test and produce a postmortem perf analysis report.
Jen Park: assigning owners: Rahul = perf analysis, Sam = admission logic, Jen = rollout + postmortem. Thanks all. Filing draft postmortem after we stabilize. :thumbsup:
